incident-bot: ALERT: High error-rate detected on /v1/chat (fn-call path). 5xx spike at 00:04 UTC, autoscaler thrash observed. Threshold: 12% -> current 28% :rotating_light:
Alex (Oncall): paging SRE oncall. I'm looking at the dashboard now — structured-output/func-call latency skyrocketed, backend GPUs queued.
Marie (SRE): I'm on it. can you confirm if this is traffic-wide or specific tenants?
Devon (Runtime): From traces it looks like long-running agent tasks + heavy JSON serialization from fn-calls. A handful of tenants account for ~70% of fn-call tokens in the last 10m.
Sam (Infra): autoscaler is flapping between 2 <-> 6 pods, NVMe cache thrash too. Need to reduce request pressure ASAP.
Alex (Oncall): proposal: temporarily block external function/tool calls and structured-output mode at the gateway for 10m while we stabilize. Prefer tenant-scoped gating if possible.
Marie (SRE): Agreed. Tenant-scoped preferable. Which tenants are highest?
Devon (Runtime): Top offenders: AcmeCorp (t-acme-21), NeonWidgets (t-nw-9), and experimental-sandbox (t-sbx-5). Acme and Neon are high-traffic; sandbox is noisy test traffic.
Olivia (CS): Heads up — AcmeCorp contacts will likely open tickets if they see degraded function calling. I'll preemptively notify them after action.
Alex (Oncall): OK. Plan: 1) Apply per-tenant temporary gating: deny fn-call & structured output for sandbox and NeonWidgets now. 2) If errors don't drop, flip a broader global soft-deny: return 429 for fn-call requests with header X-Redwood-FnCall-Gated. 3) Keep dedicated logging and metrics.
Marie (SRE): I can run the gating commands. Devon, can you prepare the rollback steps?
Devon (Runtime): Rollback is `redwoodctl routing update --remove-gate=fncall --tenants t-nw-9,t-sbx-5` and a global `--remove-global-gate=fncall`. I'll paste exact commands in thread.
Sam (Infra): Also setting an emergency rate limit at the edge to 10 rps per tenant for chat endpoints to protect backend while gates are applied.
Alex (Oncall): Execute when ready. Keep the window minimal.
Marie (SRE): Running per-tenant gate now. CMD:
```
# gate fn-call + structured output for specific tenants
redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant t-nw-9 --set "fn_call.enabled=false" --set "structured_output.enabled=false"
redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant t-sbx-5 --set "fn_call.enabled=false" --set "structured_output.enabled=false"
```
Marie (SRE): Done. Applying edge rate limits.
Sam (Infra): Edge rule pushed. `edgectl limit create --route "/v1/chat" --tenant t-nw-9 --rps 10` and same for t-sbx-5.
incident-bot: NOTE: Change window recorded: emergency change by Marie (SRE) — gating applied.
Alex (Oncall): Observability check: token processing queue depth?
Devon (Runtime): queue depth dropped ~45% in 60s. 5xx rate falling from 28% -> 11% after 90s. Good signal.
Marie (SRE): For AcmeCorp (t-acme-21) I'm going to leave unblocked for now but mark as monitored. If we need to, we'll do a soft-deny (429) instead of hard block.
Olivia (CS): I'll message Acme's Platform contact: "We're seeing platform load and may make short-lived protective changes; will update in 10 minutes". Posting now.
Olivia (CS): Sent to Acme: they've replied: 'please minimize impact on production; if you must block, whitelist our tenant or route non-fn-call fallback'.
Alex (Oncall): Devon, can we quickly provide Acme with a fallback: respond with structured text only (no tool invoking) by header override?
Devon (Runtime): Yes — we can enable header `X-Redwood-Force-Text=true` for t-acme-21. Two commands:
```
# soft fallback for Acme
redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant t-acme-21 --set "fn_call.enabled=true" --set "runtime.fallback_to_text=true"
```
Devon (Runtime): Applied. This keeps fn_call.enabled but forces the runtime to avoid external tool invocation when heuristics would call them.
Marie (SRE): Good. Metrics show overall 5xx now 6% and CPU on GPUs stabilizing. Autoscaler cooled to 3 pods.
Sam (Infra): I'll keep edge rate limits in place for 15m and then re-evaluate.
Alex (Oncall): Can we also bump quotas temporarily for some latency-sensitive tenants to reduce retry storms? That seems counterintuitive but customers were retrying a lot.
Marie (SRE): We can increase short-term token quotas for priority tenants (Acme) to reduce client-side retries. Do it only for Acme.
Sam (Infra): Done: `quotactl adjust --tenant t-acme-21 --token-burst 2x --duration 10m`.
Olivia (CS): Acme ack'd the fallback change and appreciates the heads-up. They asked for postmortem and ETA for full restore. I'll coordinate.
Devon (Runtime): Next steps: 1) keep gates for t-nw-9 and t-sbx-5 for 10m, 2) monitor error/latency curves and revert in safe window, 3) schedule a follow-up to root cause noisy agent loops and improve per-tenant throttles.
Alex (Oncall): Noted. If metrics stay good in 10m, we will remove tenant gates and edge limits.
Marie (SRE): I'll start a quick runbook entry for the change and a tag for the postmortem. Recording commands and timelines.
ops-bot: CHANGELOG: emergency-1859991234 -> gated fn-call for t-nw-9,t-sbx-5; soft-fallback for t-acme-21; edge limits applied.
Alex (Oncall): Alright team — looks stable. I'll hand off to next oncall at +30m. Please leave notes in the incident doc.
Marie (SRE): Leaving note: observed root cause likely runaway tool callback loops in sandbox tests + heuristic mismatch that escalates structured-output generation; will include mitigation suggestions: tenant QoS, per-tenant circuit breakers, and controlled fn-call budget.
Olivia (CS): I'll follow up with impacted customers and summarize actions + ETA for full restore.
Devon (Runtime): Rolling back gates now as error rate is under threshold. Commands: `redwoodctl tenant config set --tenant t-nw-9 --set "fn_call.enabled=true" --set "structured_output.enabled=true"` and remove edge limits.
Marie (SRE): Revert done for t-nw-9 and t-sbx-5 at 00:18 UTC. Edge limits removed 00:19 UTC.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: noise reduced, error-rate back to baseline. Duration ~15m.
Alex (Oncall): Closing thread. Filed postmortem ticket INC-2026-185999 with notes. Thanks everyone. :party-parrot:
